newsitem.title: FINLAND: HK SAYS SATISFIED WITH SHARE PRICE.
newsitem.headline: HK SAYS SATISFIED WITH SHARE PRICE.

text.p: Finnish food group HK Ruokatalo Oy said it was satisfied with the valuation of its shares on the first day of trade on the Helsinki Brokers' list.

"It is quite a realistic price compared to the group's earnings potential," HK Ruokatalo finance director Jukka Ahonen told Reuters by telephone, when asked for comment on the company's 119.00 markka share price on Thursday afternoon.
"The price is good and to some extent in line with our expectations," he added, but declined to estimate HK Ruokatalo's 1996 price to earnings ratio at the 119 markka share price.

HK Ruokatalo has not yet released its 1996 earnings in figures, but said last week that its full-year 1996 result would be positive. In 1995, HK Ruokatalo's predecessor LSO Foods had a 35 million markka profit before extraordinary items.

The first deal in HK Ruokatalo shares on Thursday was an in-house deal of 495,500 shares at 100.00 markka per share by Opstock. HK announced later that its main owner LSO cooperative had lowered its holding to 63.0 percent of shares from 83.7 percent.
The biggest buyer in the 49.6 million markka deal was Kuntien Elakevakuutus which acquired 6.25 percent of HK's shares, Ahonen said.
Among big buyers were also insurance companies ~Nova~, ~Elake-Varma~, Sampo and mutual funds of brokerages AG Private Bankers, FIM Securities and Aktia, he said.
Ahonen said LS could "in the long run" further lower its stake in HK to about 50 percent of shares.
